items.stem: A user reports their computer is 'slow'. What is the best first troubleshooting step?

options.text: Gather specific details about when and how the slowness occurs
options.rationale: Correct: defining the problem precisely guides every later step.
A full reinstall is drastic and premature before the cause is known.
Replacing hardware before diagnosis risks wasted cost and effort.

options.text: Tell the user to buy a new computer
options.rationale: This skips diagnosis entirely and does not resolve the ticket.

items.explanation: Correct: establishing the exact problem is the first step of a structured method.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO actions belong in a good ticket resolution note? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The root cause that was identified
options.rationale: Correct: the cause lets the next technician recognise a repeat.

options.text: The exact steps taken to fix it
options.rationale: Correct: reproducible steps make the fix reusable.

options.text: A guess about what might be wrong next time
options.rationale: Speculation without evidence is not a resolution record.

options.text: The user's personal opinion of the IT team
options.rationale: Irrelevant to resolving or documenting the incident.

items.explanation: Correct: a resolution note records the cause and the steps taken.

items.stem: ping to the default gateway succeeds but a website will not load. What does this most likely indicate?

options.text: Local link to the gateway is fine; the issue is likely DNS or beyond the gateway
options.rationale: Correct: reaching the gateway isolates the fault to name resolution or upstream.
An unplugged cable would normally stop the gateway ping too.
Display hardware is unrelated to network reachability.
Input drivers do not affect gateway reachability.

items.explanation: Correct: a successful gateway ping points to DNS or upstream rather than the local link.
